The CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' for scripts which defeats much of the security benefit of CSP. While this may be necessary for the playground's dynamic code execution, it leaves users vulnerable to XSS if AI-generated HTML contains malicious scripts. Consider documenting this security tradeoff or implementing additional validation on the generated HTML.
```suggestion
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'none'; script-src 'unsafe-inline' https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com https://unpkg.com https://esm.sh; style-src 'unsafe-inline' https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com https://unpkg.com https://esm.sh https://fonts.googleapis.com; img-src data: blob: https:; font-src https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com https://fonts.googleapis.com https://fonts.gstatic.com; connect-src https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com https://unpkg.com https://esm.sh">
```

The sandbox message handler (line 162) does not validate event.origin. All messages from any origin are processed if they have the correct structure. This should verify the message comes from the parent window or a trusted origin to prevent malicious scripts in the generated HTML from triggering unauthorized actions.

The `sync` variable is imported and obtained from useSync() but never used in the playground context. This creates an unnecessary dependency on SyncProvider. Either remove the unused import and variable, or document why it's needed even though it's not directly referenced.

Multiple postMessage calls in the sandbox use wildcard "*" targetOrigin (lines 106, 141, 252, 266, 303, 340). This allows any window to receive these messages, including messages that might contain user prompts or error information. Since this code runs in a sandboxed iframe loaded via srcdoc, you should use a specific origin or verify the parent's origin before posting sensitive data.

The auto-fix logic triggers automatically when an error occurs (up to 3 times). This could create an infinite loop of API calls if the AI consistently generates broken code. The error is still displayed to the user while the fix is being attempted, which could be confusing. Consider adding a delay, user confirmation, or more visible indication that auto-fix is in progress.

When a window is closed, if it was selected, the code sets selected to windows[0]?.id on line 117. However, this reads from store.windows which still contains the window being deleted (the produce hasn't applied yet). This will select the wrong window. You should read from the updated windows array inside the produce callback or use a different index.

The postMessage call uses wildcard "*" for targetOrigin, which allows messages to be intercepted by any window that can access this iframe. This exposes AI requests and user data to potential security risks. Use a specific origin or the parent's origin instead.
```suggestion
  const targetOrigin =
    config.iframe.src
      ? new URL(config.iframe.src, window.location.href).origin
      : window.location.origin

  function post(msg: ToSandbox) {
    if (disposed) return
    config.iframe.contentWindow?.postMessage(msg, targetOrigin)
```

The collectResponse function creates event listeners (unsub and unsub2) but only cleans them up in the success/error paths. If the promise is never resolved or rejected (edge case), these listeners will leak. Consider adding cleanup in a finally block or using AbortController to ensure listeners are always removed.

The timeout at line 194 resolves with partial text after 60 seconds, but doesn't call unsub2(). This will leave the session.status event listener active, causing a memory leak. Both unsub() and unsub2() should be called in the timeout handler.

The iframe sandbox attribute only includes "allow-scripts" which is very restrictive. However, the CSP in the sandbox HTML allows connect-src to CDNs, implying that scripts should be able to make network requests. The sandbox should also include "allow-same-origin" to enable fetch/XHR, or the CSP connect-src directive should be removed to match the restrictive sandbox. The current configuration creates an inconsistency.
```suggestion
        sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin"
```

The saveFilePickerDialog path is obtained but never used. The code comment on line 41 says "for now use blob download" but the blob download always executes regardless of whether a path was selected. Either implement the desktop file writing or remove the unused saveFilePickerDialog call to avoid confusing users with a file picker that doesn't actually save to the selected location.

The debounce timeout is not cleaned up when the component unmounts. If the user switches windows or closes the drawer while a timeout is pending, it will still fire and update the wrong window. Add cleanup in an onCleanup hook to clear the timeout.

The createSandboxListener does not validate event.origin before processing messages. Any iframe or window on the page could send crafted messages to trigger actions. You should verify that event.origin matches expected origins or that the source is a known iframe contentWindow.

The magic number `0x00000010` should be replaced with a named constant for clarity and maintainability. This value represents `CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE`, which should be imported from `windows_sys::Win32::System::Threading` similar to how `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` and `CREATE_SUSPENDED` are used elsewhere in the codebase. Using named constants makes the code more readable and helps prevent errors.

**Behavior change: regex is now stricter.**

The old local regex was:
```
/^(feat|fix|...)\s*(\([a-zA-Z0-9-]+\))?\s*:/
```
The shared action's default is:
```
/^(type)(\([\w-]+\))?!?:\s+.+$/
```
Differences:
1. Requires a non-empty subject after ``: `` (old allowed bare `feat:`)
2. Disallows space before colon (old allowed `feat :`)
3. Adds `!` (breaking-change marker) support
4. `\w` in scope also matches digits/underscore, while old was `[a-zA-Z0-9-]`

This is a good tightening but is an undocumented behavior change for contributors. Consider adding a comment here noting the regex change, or a `CHANGELOG` entry.

**`skip-users` input is unused — dual maintenance risk.**

The shared action accepts a `skip-users` input that performs the same exclusion as the job-level `if` condition. Currently, the skip list (andreiships, opencode-agent[bot]) is maintained only in the `if` condition. If a future maintainer adds a user to `skip-users:` here without also updating the `if`, the job will still run but the action will skip internally — silently diverging.

Recommendation: either document that skip-users is intentionally unused (the job-level `if` is the single source of truth), or migrate to `skip-users` input and remove the job-level condition.

**`core.setFailed()` step name is misleading on failure.**

When title validation fails, the step that appears failed in the GitHub Actions UI will be `Manage PR labels and check linked issue`, not something that says `PR title invalid`. This is confusing for PR authors trying to understand why their PR check failed.

The shared action step name `Validate PR Title` would have shown the failure clearly if `continue-on-error` were not set. Consider renaming this step to `Validate PR and manage labels` or similar so the failure surface is more descriptive.

The `maxProjectWidth` calculation on line 138 is performed even when `all` is false/undefined, meaning it's computed but never used. Consider moving this calculation inside the conditional block where `all` is true to avoid unnecessary computation when displaying the default table format.
Good call. Addressed in 4eb27557f: `maxProjectWidth` is now computed only when `--all` is enabled.

Using `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` env vars can be unset (or even empty) in some launch contexts (notably GUI apps), which would silently leave the process working directory unchanged and undermine the goal of avoiding `/` as the CWD. This crate already depends on `dirs` and uses `dirs::home_dir()` elsewhere; consider switching to `dirs::home_dir()` (and/or filtering out empty values) and only calling `current_dir` when the resolved path exists/is a directory.

Adding `.github/TEAM_MEMBERS` as a path trigger for hash regeneration is misleading: since `packages/script/src/index.ts` doesn't currently read this file during the `bun install` build phase, changes to TEAM_MEMBERS will not produce a different `node_modules` output hash. This trigger will cause the hash-regeneration workflow to run when TEAM_MEMBERS changes, but it will always produce the same hash and result in a no-op commit. If this file is genuinely not used by the build, this path should not be listed here.
```suggestion

```

The PR description states that `packages/script/src/index.ts` reads `.github/TEAM_MEMBERS` at build time (citing PR #15369), and the linked issue #15400 includes a code snippet showing a `Bun.file(teamPath).text()` call. However, the actual current content of `packages/script/src/index.ts` still uses a hardcoded team array (lines 49–66) and does not read `.github/TEAM_MEMBERS` at all. If this fix is pre-emptive and anticipates a future code change, the PR description should make that clear. If PR #15369 was supposed to add that file-reading logic, it either hasn't been merged yet or was reverted.

As a result they won’t be usable via the typed i18n API (t(key: Key, ...)) and may even fail type-checking depending on how excess properties are handled. ```

That means they can’t be referenced through the typed i18n helper (t(key: Key, ...)) and will be effectively unreachable (or cause type errors elsewhere if referenced). Please add the corresponding keys to packages/console/app/src/i18n/en.ts first, then keep tr.ts as an override for those keys.

`createEffect(on(retry, ..., { defer: true }))` will not run on initial mount. If the SessionRetry component mounts while the session is already in `status.type === "retry"` (e.g. opening an in-progress session), the interval never starts and the countdown won't update. Consider removing `defer: true` so the effect runs once on mount and sets up the timer when `retry()` is initially truthy.

`register()` sets `iconPath` and `followupProvider` on the internal `vscode.ChatParticipant`, but the public `iconPath` / `followupProvider` fields on `OpenCodeChatParticipant` are never assigned. This makes those properties always `undefined` (and the unit tests that read them will fail). Either remove these fields, or assign them in `register()` and keep them in sync with `this.participant`.
```suggestion

    const iconPath = vscode.Uri.file(this.context.asAbsolutePath("images/icon.png"))
    const followupProvider = this.createFollowupProvider()

    this.iconPath = iconPath
    this.followupProvider = followupProvider

    this.participant.iconPath = iconPath
    this.participant.followupProvider = followupProvider
```

`setupStreaming` registers a new `client.onSessionUpdate` listener on every `handle()` call, but never unregisters it. Over multiple chat turns this will accumulate listeners and duplicate streaming output (and leak memory). Prefer registering once per handler instance and routing by sessionId, or change `AcpClient.onSessionUpdate` to return a disposable/unsubscribe function and dispose it when the request completes.

`handleProcessCrash` changes controller state and shows a warning, but it doesn't actually re-initialize `JsonRpcConnection`/`AcpClient` after an `AcpProcess` restart. Since `AcpProcess` can auto-restart internally, the controller will keep a connection/client wired to the old stdio streams and future requests will fail. Consider handling `process.onRestart`/`onSpawn` to rebuild the connection/client, or disable internal auto-restart and perform a full restart sequence here (including awaiting `cleanup()`).
```suggestion
    // Treat any crash as a hard failure: move to ERROR and clean up resources.
    this.state = ActivationState.ERROR
    this.cleanup()

    vscode.window.showWarningMessage("OpenCode process crashed and has been stopped.")
```

`openNewTerminalDisposable` is created but never added to `context.subscriptions`, so it won't be disposed on extension deactivation/reload. Add it to the `context.subscriptions.push(...)` call alongside the other command disposables.
```suggestion
  context.subscriptions.push(openNewTerminalDisposable, openTerminalDisposable, addFilepathDisposable)
```

This config imports `configureVirtualLab` but never uses it, which will fail linting under typical ESLint rules. Also, the `label` "unit" is duplicated for two entries; if the test runner expects unique labels, one of these may be ignored/overwritten. Consider removing the unused import and giving each config a distinct label (or merging the `files` globs).

`handleChatRequest` calls `ensureActivated()` but then ignores the returned client and responds with hard-coded markdown. This doesn't match the stated goal of streaming ACP responses and persisting sessions. Consider wiring `OpenCodeRequestHandler` (and session/storage management) into this participant so non-command requests are sent to ACP and streamed back via `ChatResponseStream`.

`bufferMessage` calls `flushBuffer(null as any)` when the buffer exceeds 10 chunks. Since `flushBuffer` clears `messageBuffer` and only writes when `stream` is non-null, this drops content for longer responses (anything beyond ~10 chunks). Pass the active `stream` into `bufferMessage`/`flushBuffer`, or remove this early flush and instead flush on a timer or after each chunk.

`MockAcpServer` doesn't appear to match the ACP protocol implemented by `AcpClient`/`protocol.ts`: it returns `protocolVersion` as a string and uses method names like `session/start`/`session/end` rather than `session/new`/`session/prompt`/`session/load`. This means integration tests based on this server won't validate the real wire protocol. Align the mock server's method names and response shapes with `sdks/vscode/src/acp/protocol.ts`.

`atomicWrite` is not actually atomic: it writes a temp file, then deletes the destination, then writes the destination again. A crash between delete/write can lose the previous file entirely. VS Code's `FileSystem` API does provide `rename(source, target, { overwrite: true })`; use that to replace the target in a single operation (and keep the temp file in the same directory), or otherwise avoid deleting the destination before the new content is durably written.
```suggestion
      // Atomically replace the target file by renaming the temp file
      await this.fs.rename(tempUri, uri, { overwrite: true })
```

`isFileNotFound`/`isFileExists` rely on substring matching in `error.message` (e.g. "ENOENT", "already exists"). VS Code file APIs typically throw `vscode.FileSystemError` with structured codes; checking message text is brittle across OS/locales. Prefer detecting `error instanceof vscode.FileSystemError` and checking `error.code` (or comparing against `vscode.FileSystemError.FileNotFound(...)` patterns) so the behavior is consistent on Windows/Linux/macOS.

This module uses the same workspaceState key (`opencode.sessions`) as `OpenCodeStorage`, but it stores a *different schema* (a `Record<string, SessionMetadata>` here vs `{version, sessions: SessionMetadata[]}` in `storage.ts`). Mixing these will corrupt session persistence depending on which code runs last. Please consolidate on one schema/key (ideally via `OpenCodeStorage`) or change one of the keys to avoid collisions.

`error` is a single global signal, but it’s rendered inside each plugin card. If saving one plugin fails, the error message will appear under every plugin card. Consider tracking error state per `pluginId` (similar to `saving`) or moving the error rendering outside the per-plugin loop. ```suggestion )}

`schemas` is treated as trusted data (typed as `PluginSchema[]`), but the API response is not validated and `schema.properties` is assumed to be a plain object. A malformed plugin (or unexpected server response) can throw at `Object.entries(schema.properties)` and break the whole settings page. Consider validating/normalizing the response (e.g., with a Zod schema) and skipping/flagging invalid schemas instead of rendering them blindly.

The response schema for `schemas` is `z.array(z.unknown())`, which means the OpenAPI spec (and generated SDK types) can’t describe plugin settings schemas and provides no runtime validation. Consider defining a Zod schema for `PluginSettingsSchema` (id/title/properties with SettingDefinition) and using it here so clients get proper typing and the server rejects malformed plugin schemas.

`SettingDefinition` is a single shape for all field types, so TypeScript allows invalid combinations (e.g., `type: "select"` without `enum`, or `enum` on a `boolean`). Since the UI relies on fields like `enum` for selects, consider switching to a discriminated union keyed by `type` to make invalid schemas a compile-time error for plugin authors.
```suggestion
type BaseSettingDefinition<TType extends string, TValue> = {
  type: TType
  title: string
  description?: string
  default?: TValue
  required?: boolean
  placeholder?: string
}

export type StringSettingDefinition = BaseSettingDefinition<"string", string>

export type NumberSettingDefinition = BaseSettingDefinition<"number", number>

export type BooleanSettingDefinition = BaseSettingDefinition<"boolean", boolean>

export type SelectSettingDefinition = BaseSettingDefinition<"select", string> & {
  enum: string[]
  enumLabels?: string[]
}

export type SecretSettingDefinition = BaseSettingDefinition<"secret", string>

export type SettingDefinition =
  | StringSettingDefinition
  | NumberSettingDefinition
  | BooleanSettingDefinition
  | SelectSettingDefinition
  | SecretSettingDefinition
```

Any plugin that returns object/array settings will render rows with no input control (and can’t be edited). This generated client method doesn’t expose the new `scope` field supported by `PATCH /config/plugin-settings`, and also makes `plugin_id` / `settings` optional even though the endpoint validator requires them. Regenerating from an up-to-date OpenAPI spec should add `scope?: "global" | "project"` and make required fields required in the method signature.
